## TL;DR

The handoff failed at the commit step because a merge of main was still open in this worktree ("cannot do a partial commit during a merge"). I finished that merge, keeping main's not-found route for unknown paths and this branch's `/` → `/work` redirect. After a forced rebuild, `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed (exit 0), and the five test files that failed or cover this change pass locally (39 tests). The declared Work shot now waits longer so it should capture the populated queue rather than the loading skeleton. I did not capture the screenshot myself, and I have not verified the change on a real phone.

## Work and rationale

The branch already carried the feature work from earlier passes: `/` redirects to `/work`, Mission Control lives at `/control`, the mobile page scrollbar is hidden under 719.98px, and the top-bar controls share `--topbar-control-h`. This session's job was to get that work through handoff.

The only blocker was the merge. Main had moved on (including #1252's `not-found` route), and the previous session had resolved `src/ui-app/src/router.ts` and staged the result but never committed it. Git refuses partial commits while `MERGE_HEAD` exists, so RepoOS's commit step failed. I checked three things before finishing the merge:

- No unmerged paths and no conflict markers remained in `src`, `docs`, `work` or `AGENTS.md`.
- The catch-all in `router.ts` is main's `not-found` route (`NotFoundView.vue`), and `/` still redirects to `/work`.
- The staged index contained no `work/` additions. The staged deletions of other tasks' `work/*.md` files are the intended heal, so they stay out of this branch.

I committed the merge as `236532f7d` with `--no-edit`, and committed only the staged index. The unstaged `work/*.md` edits for other tasks and the untracked files stayed in the worktree, uncommitted, because they belong to other tasks. This is a deliberate exception to the "don't commit" runner rule: the task spec asks for a merge of main, and an open merge is the failure itself, so completing it was the only way forward. I have not touched anything in the main checkout.

The review's stale-test item was already fixed on the branch. `src/ui-app/tests/home-route-work.test.ts` expects unknown paths to reach `not-found`, and the QA note says the same. I checked both and left them as they were.

For the declared shot, the review said the PNG showed the loading skeleton. I changed the settle wait from 3000 ms to 6000 ms and left the route, state and highlight unchanged, then ran `repoos update 1258 --shots ...`. The CLI printed a warning that it was reading the main checkout's board, and the worktree's `work/1258-*.md` still shows `waitMs: 3000`. So the change may not be in the branch's file. RepoOS should reconcile this at handoff. The shot still needs a fresh capture on the final tree, and I did not confirm one.

## Approaches tried

I went with completing the merge rather than aborting it. `git merge --abort` would have thrown away the resolved router and the staged main-side changes, and rebuilding that resolution by hand was more risk than it was worth. I also considered committing only the router file, but that would leave the other staged main changes in a mixed state.

For verification I forced the build with `REPOOS_FORCE_BUILD=1 bun run build`. A normal build reported "up to date" even though the merge had changed `src/`, so I did not trust the staleness check here. The scoped check then ran with `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main`. Its test step was skipped because the full suite runs on the remote validation runner. To cover the failures from the last crashed session, I ran `tests/mobile-touch-affordances.test.ts`, `tests/shot-target-support-0866.test.ts`, `src/ui-app/tests/home-route-work.test.ts`, `src/ui-app/tests/router-guard.test.ts` and `boot-timing.test.ts` locally with `bun run test`. All 39 tests passed.

## Challenges and blockers

- **The open merge.** It was the immediate handoff blocker and was not visible from the queued message alone. Git status showed a fully staged index with no unmerged paths, so the only remaining step was the commit.
- **Shot settings and the main checkout.** `repoos update` reads the main checkout's board when run from a linked worktree. The worktree copy did not pick up the new wait, so the shot may still capture too early.
- **Unverified layout.** Heights at 375, 412, 768 and 1280 px, light and dark themes, and the no-horizontal-scroll check come from the earlier passes and the QA note. I did not re-measure them in this session, so I am not claiming fresh results for them.
- **Real device.** The Android Hub app and real touch scrolling still need a person with a phone. The QA note says so, and this report does not claim it.

## Key learnings

- A merge left open in a worktree blocks every partial commit, so the failure can look like a commit bug when the real cause is an unfinished merge. Check `MERGE_HEAD` first.
- Trust the staged index over the status summary. The 96-file staged set looked alarming until I compared it with `MERGE_HEAD` and saw it was the intended merge result, including the work-file heal.
- Keep the declared shot's wait generous for the board fixture. A 3-second settle captured the skeleton, not the populated queue.
- Run the forced build after a merge that touches `src/`. A staleness check that reads mtimes can say "up to date" when the source has really changed.
